channel.title: Butch Mahinay
channel.description: New blog posts and Python for Treasury Work lessons by Butch Mahinay

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 7: Keep Money in Its Fund
item.description: A peso raised for schools should reach schools. Each peso belongs to the fund the law assigns it, and it should stay there.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 6: Separate the Hands
item.description: No one person should both approve and release public money, or both hold it and record it. Trust in a treasury has to be designed, not assumed.

item.title: Lesson 8: Check a collections file before you trust it
item.description: Catch blank payors, impossible dates, mistyped funds, commas in amounts and extra decimals, and list every problem by line.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 5: Every Record Has a Seal
item.description: Once a record is posted, it can be corrected, but only in the open: with a reason, a name and a trace that anyone can check.

item.title: Cybersecurity Series, Part 3: The Art of Human Hacking
item.description: Most scams do not break into computers; they persuade people. Learn the pressure tricks behind phishing, smishing, fake bosses and deepfake calls, and the simple rules that stop them.

item.title: First Class or Fifth? How a Local Government’s Income Class Is Decided, and Why It Matters
item.description: Every province, city and municipality in the Philippines carries an income class, from first to fifth. This post explains how the Automatic Income Classification Act (RA 11964) sets that class, what income is counted, and how moving up a class can change both salaries and the personal services limit.

item.title: Project Management Series, Part 2: The Project Charter on One Page
item.description: A project charter is a short document that says why a project exists, what it will deliver, who is in charge and who approved it. This post shows how to write one on a single page, using a treasury encoding project as the example.

item.title: Data Analytics Series, Part 2: The Six Steps of Every Analysis
item.description: Ask, Prepare, Process, Analyze, Share and Act. Each step comes with the mistake that follows when it is skipped, and one worked example runs through all six: does a treasury office need a second payment window?

item.title: Business Intelligence Series, Part 2: The BI Team, Role by Role
item.description: Behind every dashboard that people trust are three kinds of work: building the pipes, building the screens and explaining what the numbers mean. Each role is explained in plain words, along with how one person in a small treasury can wear all three hats.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 4: Every Owner Has a Deadline
item.description: A deadline is not paperwork. It sets a limit on how long a mistake or a shortage can stay hidden.

item.title: Cybersecurity Series, Part 2: Identity Is the New Perimeter
item.description: Attackers no longer break in; they log in. That is why long passphrases beat complex passwords, why a password manager helps, which kinds of two-step login are strongest, and why passkeys are coming.

item.title: Business Intelligence Series, Part 1: Same Data, Different Jobs
item.description: Business intelligence and data analytics use the same records but do different jobs. This post covers what BI really means, where the name came from, what a BI system is made of, and how a monthly treasury report can stop being rebuilt by hand.

item.title: Lesson 7: Keep a receipts register in SQLite
item.description: Save official receipts in a small database file, total them with SQL, and let the database itself refuse a duplicate OR number.

item.title: Data Analytics Series, Part 1: What Data Analytics Really Is, and Why Every Office Already Has the Data
item.description: Data analytics is the craft of turning everyday records into answers people can act on. Along the way: the four kinds of questions it can answer, a famous cholera map from 1854, and why a local treasury already sits on a mountain of useful data.

item.title: Project Management Series, Part 1: The Accidental Project Manager in the Treasury
item.description: A project can land on your desk without the title. Learn how a project differs from daily work, the three limits every project lives with, and four moves to make in your first two weeks.

item.title: Lesson 6: Make a formatted Excel report with openpyxl
item.description: Turn the day's receipts into a real Excel file with a bold header, peso formatting, a SUM formula and a frozen top row.

item.title: Year-End in the Treasury: What Really Happens in December
item.description: While most offices slow down for Christmas, the local treasury speeds up. December brings bonuses, last-minute vouchers, unspent budgets and cash counts, and the office must also get ready for the January rush.

item.title: Your Data at the Treasury Counter: What an Office May Share, and What It Must Protect
item.description: Every payment at the town hall leaves a trail of personal information. The Data Privacy Act decides what an office may share and what it must protect, and a few simple habits keep taxpayers safe.

item.title: Cybersecurity Series, Part 1: How Modern Cyberattacks Really Work
item.description: Forget the hoodie-wearing genius. Today's cyberattacks are run like businesses. Learn what security protects, who the attackers are, how a breach unfolds step by step, and why layered defenses work.

item.title: How to Use the RPT Calculator: Know Your Amilyar Before You Pay
item.description: A step-by-step guide to the free Real Property Tax Calculator on this site, with worked examples, and the lessons every property owner should know about discounts, interest and where the money goes.

item.title: Lesson 2: Check an official receipt series for gaps and duplicates
item.description: Compare the receipts recorded today with the booklet issued, and flag missing, repeated or stray numbers.

item.title: Lesson 3: Compute real property tax penalties with Decimal
item.description: See why floats are unsafe for money, then compute 2% monthly penalties with a 36-month cap, rounded correctly.

item.title: Lesson 4: Build a simple RCD summary with pandas
item.description: Group collections by collector and fund, list the receipts used, and match collections against deposits.

item.title: Lesson 5: Make a tamper-evident log with HMAC
item.description: Seal each log entry with a keyed hash chained to the one before it, so any later edit or deletion shows.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 3: Every Document Has an Owner
item.description: A receipt that belongs to everyone belongs to no one. Every form in custody and every peso in hand needs a named, bonded officer who answers for it.

item.title: Lesson 1: Add up a day's collections from a CSV file
item.description: Read the day's official receipts from a spreadsheet export and total them per fund, to the centavo.

item.title: So Close to Alibijaban Island
item.description: On Hermano Puli Day, I sat alone on someone else's bangka in San Andres, Quezon, and looked out at an island I have loved for almost two decades. This time, I could not cross.

item.title: Why .dev and Not .com: How I Chose My Website's Address
item.description: Most people expect a .com. I chose aumahinay.dev. I explain why, in plain words, and what it taught me about building things that are safe by default.

item.title: 200 Kilometers and Five Years Later: Coming Home to the Farm
item.description: Five years. That is how long it had been since I last set foot on my 3-hectare farm.

item.title: Lesson 0: Getting started: install Python and run your first script
item.description: Install Python on Windows or Mac, open the command line, and run a script, with fixes for the usual first errors.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 2: Every Peso Has a Document
item.description: No collection without an accountable form, no release without a voucher. A peso that leaves no paper behind cannot be accounted for.

item.title: 360 Degrees: My First Post as Acting Municipal Treasurer
item.description: Two years, two Mayors, a pandemic, a typhoon and an election: what my first post as Acting Municipal Treasurer of a municipality in Quezon taught me.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 1: Legality First
item.description: Before we ask how a peso was handled, we should ask whether the law allowed it at all.

item.title: Why I Built ALTOS: Bringing Automation to Philippine Local Treasuries
item.description: A treasury system built around one idea: every peso should be accounted for from the moment it arrives to the moment it is reported.
